cases.why_previous_did_not_resolve: HeapWalk BUSY and REGION are different from PSAPI PrivateUsage; former only reports current blocks/selected regions. Prior ETW saved truncated top25 module frame occurrences, not matched allocation+free bytes or a complete call-site owner. Unproven worker quiescence biases endpoints. The corrected #45040046000 probe closes pre-workload event-start, circular overwrite, and missing local-symbol setup ONLY on a synthetic fixture. The filtered report has not yet been independently parsed into exact 16 outstanding / 5760 requested bytes and matching source stack, nor adapted to real GIO workload and global worker quiet boundary. Follow-up diagnosed that this WPT version's combined `-stacks -size 360 361` yielded no stack frames although unfiltered `-stacks -top 100` contained the synthetic symbol. `-totals -size ... -requireframes` did not isolate source count (e.g., 84 vs known64). Local parser now verifies unfiltered unique-source stack 64/16, so that synthetic gap is FIXED. No proof yet of true GIO owner across completed worker epochs. The watch subscription submechanism IS NOW bounded by both pinned source and runtime counts; previously only a source-level model had been available. It cannot explain the remaining owner-unknown GIO/WinRT and COM/heap commit residuals. Do not rerun watch bound as if unproven. Existing 256/512MB full-registry sequential ETW stopped HeapSession before safe stop, making owner inference impossible. New last4-of16 capture fixed logger exhaustion but revealed an Xperf source stack report shape/coverage difference. Previous parser did not preserve a safe error classification or independently extract aggregate Out# on failure; this is a diagnostic-instrument limitation, not a proven leak or an unexplained endpoint. Two genuine registry late-window captures are now available, unlike the earlier missing HeapSession. Full stack attribution still failed because 31 of 1024 Xperf rows reported Out#>Alloc# and top-1024 count was saturated; a further 466 outstanding blocks cannot be assigned to a validated stack. This is no longer generic 'unknown': specific Xperf row semantics and top-N truncation are the active diagnostic defects. The independent Xperf heap totals DO establish 16061 outstanding in both runs, not their expected lifetime. Avoid treating bad rows as OTHER or silently accepting out>alloc. The top-frame-image fallback does not match Xperf total/stack output; sanitized diagnostics #45059995357 show global_headers=0,top_headers=0,alloc_lines=0,one dash part. Thus treating its absence as no images would be false. 15595 source-GIO-containing stack live counts are real during incomplete lifetime; after_cleanup had active AppInfo worker, so no proof they had outlived intended work. Private0→16 and ETW13→16 cannot be causally subtracted. New QPC observation #45062227506 excludes observed GIO rebuild-worker overlap at Xperf stop within THIS instrumented process, but cannot identify the 466 blocks because 30 rows violate Out<=Alloc and the top1024 limit was reached; xperf -images returned unsupported report shape. Its same-run resource deltas cover cycles0-16 while ETW late4 covers 13-16, and logging changed workload timing. The 466 was incorrectly conflated with omitted top1024 stack rows: expanded -top8192 group inventory shows 1164 total groups and no additional Out, while exactly 30 raw zero-Alloc positive-Out groups sum 466. These were rejected by our simplistic Out<=Alloc per-call-stack invariant. The Xperf stack-report groups may reflect HeapReAlloc or other attribution semantics; these hypotheses are not proven without independent allocation/free lifetime matching. Earlier parser falsely required each stack row Out<=Alloc. Genuine synthetic #45133407278 proves that realloc stack can legitimately have Alloc0/Realloc16/Out16. Actual GIO #45133754345 measured 31 rows Alloc0/Realloc3604/Out466, every row realloc compatible, full1166 group totals reconcile with global Alloc/Out; top1024 incompleteness and prior false numeric invariant do not explain the remaining lifetime/causal owner issue. Previously only stack-group aggregation and synthetic dicts were checked; no real ETW payload owner-chain decoder existed. The first actual decoder discarded the original owner on a HeapFree immediately before the corresponding HeapReAlloc, proven by real event counts. Corrected with bounded provisional-free link by heap+old address+oldsize, maximum 32 intervening heap events (actual distance1), address reuse collision and duplicate guards; validated actual 16 held and later freed. GIO source/lifetime remains unproven independently. All-watches-zero as a live 24/7 recorder closure gate was conceptually wrong: GLib intentionally maintains long-lived registry subscriptions and immediately rearms on notifications, so a stable six pending in both tested arms is a legitimate subscribed baseline, not an empty process-wide producer epoch. Stable watcher count and increasing PrivateUsage coexist, so neither proves the other. Prior native heap ETW parser only selected 360/720 B; a new generic size-independent state machine and real ETW mixed-size fixture passed 24/6/24 full lifetime. It additionally proved that when a foreign-size allocation reuses a previously freed heap address, the previous original identity must be retired without assigning it to the foreign new object. Native process teardown ETW events must not be confused with explicit application frees; the new dedicated native fixture signals after final free and stays alive until the ETW cut. However ETW heap Source is allocator path, not a GLib function; real original call stack is still missing. Last milestone tracked arbitrary-size original addresses but did not know any ORIGINAL allocating method. The new ETLX stack resolver explicitly symbolized a locally built native fixture and verified *the original allocating function*, not the later realloc call or heap allocator's LFH/Source path, then carried the method-proven token across realloc/free. This removes the generic parser's native fixture source-identity gap but still cannot identify actual GLib/GIO allocation functions from the earlier late4 GIO ETW window (first 12 cycles were outside trace), nor can it infer persistence from synthetic final frees.

cases.why_previous_did_not_resolve: A finished AppInfo update counter does not acknowledge not-yet-delivered APCs or globally drain other async producers. Timed wait and GObject count alone can produce false leak/plateau conclusions. Even an observed per-key watch count bound is not a closed producer queue or worker quiescence acknowledgment. Watch counts quantify one source cohort only, and do not drain Windows APC or unrelated WinRT callbacks. Even though the later phase trace observed a worker actively completing after cleanup, the recorded ETW stop was earlier (precleanup), so current instrumentation cannot map each ETW-outstanding allocation to a proved finished lifetime. Another 2s idle wait is not a globally closed callback producer barrier. Previous worker_active_after_cleanup=1 did not time-align with xperf ETW stop; newer QPC fixes that specific worker overlap observation but does not close other callback producers or prove all 16252 allocations persisted after an acknowledged producer/consumer epoch. New full row count accounting does not establish producer closure or worker-exit allocation lifetime; post-stop acknowledgment cannot certify event sources/APC globally quiet. Valid realloc group schema is a different question from a closed event producer boundary. Neither the synthetic 16 retained allocs nor the measured 466 Out blocks prove all registry APC or WinRT asynchronous work was finished. A native test process exiting after a controller signal is not evidence of GIO's unrelated callbacks, registry watchers or WinRT in-flight calls being shut down. Source producer-close ACK for actual GIO remains missing. Previous plan wrongly treated 'zero pending registry watchers' as obligatory 24/7 quiet. Source deliberately maintains subscriptions; 6 baseline roots persisted even when no notification. Also g_cond_wait and QPC worker snapshots cannot exclude queued work or future APC, and the synchronous WinRT iterator cleanup does not guarantee external COM allocation cache closure. Distinguished stable active-subscribed epoch from terminal producer-close proof. The original uniform 16-held fixture stopped ETW after process exit, possibly mixing cleanup/reuse. The new source-chaperoned mixed-size fixture keeps native producer alive until the ETW cut and observes final explicit HeapFree. This solves native fixture phase purity only; real GIO's stable six watcher subscriptions are deliberately persistent and cannot be forced to zero.
cases.missing_observable: Under actual continuous operation, an independently evidenced comparable *subscribed stable phase*: bounded watch roots/pending statuses, explicit AppInfo queued+active tasks and callback completion count, callback owned package iterator return; then complete-before-workload ETW original heap allocation source ownership and frees over comparable epochs, phase-aligned PrivateUsage/REGION. A true globally producer-closed epoch remains unavailable for unmodified GLib AppInfo persistent watcher state; don't artificially require it or claim API-driven safe unwatch exists.
cases.next_automatic_action: Keep known stable six pending watch roots as a normal subscribed baseline, not globally quiet. Build comparable active AppInfo process phase with source-owned queued and active worker, registry completion/rearm counters and allocated-source stack identity; do not require terminal AP C/WinRT watcher closure in the 24/7 recorder.
